newsitem.title: BURUNDI: Army fights rebels near Burundi capital.
newsitem.headline: Army fights rebels near Burundi capital.

text.p: Burundi's army battled Hutu rebels on the outskirts of the capital using mortars and an aircraft to rocket rebel positions, witnesses said on Tuesday.

Reports from military sources said the Tutsi-dominated army was attempting to repulse an attack on the capital by the Forces for the Defence of Democracy (FDD), armed wing of the main Hutu rebel group. There was no independent confirmation of this.
Bujumbura residents said they heard mortar fire and sustained bursts of automatic gunfire in the hills east of Bujumbura for three hours on Monday and saw an army plane fire rockets into the hills.
"The operation was going on in the hills surrounding the capital," said army spokesman Mamert Sinarinzi. He gave no details.
Scores of villagers fled the hills and gathered around Bujumbura's Unity monument overlooking the city.

"In the hills we heard gunfire and explosions. When the guns stopped many people fled their homes and gathered at the Unity monument," one woman who fled from Monday's clashes said. There were "very, very many" armed rebels in the hills, she said.
"Later we saw a plane that was shooting into the hills cross three times and the fourth time we saw people on the ground shooting at it with special guns to shoot down planes.
"The plane did not come back after that," said the woman, who declined to be identified.
Shortly after it took power in a coup in July, Burundi's Tutsi-dominated army used an Italian-made light aircraft armed with rockets to strafe rebel positions close to the capital.

Military leader Pierre Buyoya announced last month that his government had signed a pre-ceasefire agreement with the main Hutu rebel group the National Council for the Defence of Democracy (CNDD) after direct talks in Rome.
Buyoya faces opposition from Tutsis fearful that ceding power to CNDD will compromise their security as well as rebels battling the army.
Last week witnesses and a senior military source said that the army killed more than 40 Hutu rebels in fighting south of the capital Bujumbura.

More than 150,000 people have been killed in massacres and a civil war between the army and rebels since October 1993, when the country's first elected Hutu president was murdered by Tutsi troops in an attempted coup.
